newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-June 5.

text.p: There are 26 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that in an authoritarian system, many officials dared not voice different opinions to their superiors because of political pressure. The paper said that not only Chief Secretary Anson Chan but all government officials and Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa himself should promise to Hong Kong people that they would do their jobs according to their conscience.

-- APPLE DAILY said that what happened in Tiananmen Square in 1989 was still in the heart of every Chinese and that Hong Kong people could never forget this period of history. Tung Chee-hwa was wrong in urging Hong Kong to put the "baggage of June 4" behind it, because the massacre was not historical baggage but rather a bloody lesson which encouraged Hong Kong and mainland people to look forward, the paper said.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said that in less than a month's time, the "one country, two systems" principle would enter a new stage. It said that the series of successes in carrying out the principle had proved its vitality and influence and that it would be suitable to solve the Taiwan issue.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that Wednesday night's vigil to commemorate the eighth anniversary of the June 4 massacre should act as a powerful incentive for a relaxed attitude by the future Special Administrative Region authorities and Beijing. The best interests of all would be served by keeping the status quo in the sensitive area of demonstrations. The SAR will get a significant international boost if it is apparent that political freedoms, which are not present in China, will be maintained here next year.
